task.role: You are a senior Python and TypeScript engineer extending PropLock AI, a FastAPI + React app built for the PayPal AI Hackathon. You write small, tested, honest code that matches the existing codebase's style.
task.goal: Build Feature 4, "Token-to-Invoice Ledger & Dispute Defense Copilot": when a tenant locks a flat, create a PayPal invoice for the security deposit and brokerage with the captured visit token already deducted; record every money event in an append-only ledger shown in an AG Grid cockpit; send reminders; answer plain-English questions about the ledger; and draft dispute responses from evidence PropLock already holds.

repository.backend: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2, Alembic, Pydantic v2, LangGraph, Groq SDK, httpx, pytest. Python 3.11 venv at backend/.venv.
repository.frontend: Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + React Router 6, plain CSS ("verified green" design system in src/styles.css).

reuse.item: backend/app/adapters/paypal.py: PayPalCatalog._access_token, PayPalError(status, debug_id), the Fake/Demo/Unconfigured twin pattern and get_paypal().
backend/app/services/outbox.py: commit the intent first, then call PayPal from a job; claim with an atomic UPDATE lease; backoff; fixed PayPal-Request-Id so retries are idempotent.
backend/app/domain/signing.py: canonical_json + HMAC with AUDIT_SECRET. Sign invoice bodies the same way.
Each Feature 1 audit's report_json holds terms.deposit and terms.brokerage_fee for that listing version. Invoices must match them.
backend/app/adapters/llm.py: Groq JSON mode + Pydantic validation + one retry; FakeLLM for tests.
api.ts (X-API-Key, readable errors), components.tsx (Pill, Ring, Icon, useLoad, CheckReport), styles.css tokens.

context.dependency: Feature 4 consumes HOLD_AUTHORIZED, HOLD_CAPTURED and HOLD_VOIDED events. Define that contract as a Pydantic LedgerEvent and add a dev-only endpoint POST /dev/ledger/simulate-capture (MANAGER role, allowed only when DEMO_MODE=true) so Feature 4 can be built and demoed before Feature 3 exists.

paypal_apis.api: generate-next-invoice-number, create draft invoice, send, remind, cancel, get, generate-qr-code. Confirm the exact request shapes, including the invoice-level discount, in the Phase 0 spike before relying on them.
verify every event with POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature using PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID.
paypal_apis.currency: Use USD in the sandbox; PayPal does not support domestic INR between Indian accounts.

tables.table: id, listing_id, version_id, audit_id, tenant_name, tenant_email, status OPEN|INVOICED|PAID|CANCELLED|DISPUTED, created_at
id, closing_id, kind, amount Numeric(12,2), currency, direction in|out|info, paypal_ref, idempotency_key UNIQUE, occurred_at, source feature3|webhook|api|manual, raw_json
id, closing_id, paypal_invoice_id UNIQUE, number, items_json, deposit, brokerage, token_deduction, total, currency, status, due_date, sent_at, paid_at, reminders_sent, signature
paypal_event_id PK, event_type, verified, received_at, processed_at, error
id, paypal_dispute_id UNIQUE, closing_id, reason, amount, status, evidence_pack_json, draft_response, approved_by, submitted_at

money_rules.rule: invoice.total = deposit + brokerage - token_captured, never negative.
deposit and brokerage must equal the signed audit's terms for that version; a different amount requires a MANAGER override with a note, recorded as a ledger entry.
The token appears as an invoice-level discount labelled with the PayPal capture id.
Balances are derived from ledger entries; never store a running balance.

modules.module: close listing → closing + ledger + outbox jobs in one commit
AG Grid cockpit, invoice drawer, dispute review

phase.name: Spike and contract
phase.step: scripts/spike_invoicing.py: create, send, get, QR code and cancel one sandbox invoice with a discount; exit 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 no keys. Record the real JSON shapes in docs/BUILD_LOG.md.
LedgerEvent contract and POST /dev/ledger/simulate-capture (MANAGER, DEMO_MODE only).

phase.name: Ledger
phase.step: Models and one Alembic migration for the five tables; upgrade/downgrade test; CHECK-constrained enums.
ledger_service.record is idempotent by idempotency_key; no update or delete code paths; corrections are reversing entries.

phase.name: Closing to invoice
phase.step: invoice_rules: draft from the signed audit and captured token; reject mismatched amounts and negative totals.
PayPal invoicing adapter with PayPal-Request-Id; PayPalError with debug_id; Fake and Demo twins; mock-HTTP tests.
POST /broker/listings/{id}/close → closing + ledger entry + create_invoice job in one commit; job chain create → send; invoice body HMAC-signed.

phase.name: Webhooks
phase.step: POST /webhooks/paypal: verify signature, store raw event, dedupe by event id, update invoice/closing and write ledger entries.

phase.name: Cockpit
phase.step: GET /ledger (broker: own closings; manager: all) and GET /closings/{id}.

AG Grid Community cockpit: status renderers matching existing pills, money columns, grouping by closing, quick filter, invoice drawer with PayPal link and QR; card fallback at phone width; light and dark.

phase.name: Reminders
phase.step: Outbox reminder jobs at due-1, due+1, due+3 days; max 3; stop when paid; each reminder is an info ledger entry.

phase.name: Ledger copilot
phase.step: Groq JSON mode → LedgerQuery (allowed fields and operators, max 500 rows), one retry, refuse write intents; answer quotes the rows used.

phase.name: Dispute defense
phase.step: Evidence pack from the signed audit (+ /verify result), check-in proof, invoice and payment trail, trust history; every item has a source id.
LLM draft that cites ids; MANAGER approves; outbox submits evidence; status from webhooks.

phase.name: Demo and docs
phase.step: scripts/demo_feature4.py: simulated capture → invoice with token deducted → sent → paid webhook → ledger PAID → dispute → evidence pack → approved response. README section and screenshots.

phases.hackathon_cut: 0.2, 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2 (Fake and Demo first), 2.3, 4.1, 4.2 (grid only). Everything else is roadmap.

constraints.must: Work on branch feature/4-invoice-ledger. One commit per step, conventional message, ending with the attribution line the environment gives you.
Every PayPal call goes through the outbox with a fixed PayPal-Request-Id; every money event becomes a ledger entry.
Money is Decimal / Numeric(12,2) end to end and travels as strings in JSON.
Tests never touch the network: Fake adapters and httpx.MockTransport only. Keep the existing 280+ tests green.
Each step ends with its tests passing and a docs/BUILD_LOG.md entry: what changed, why, key idea, how to see it, what was verified.
Match existing code: short docstrings that say why, the same naming, Pydantic schemas in app/schemas, endpoints that map service exceptions to 403/404/409/422.
constraints.never: Never update or delete a ledger entry.
Never let an LLM call a tool that moves money, sends an invoice or submits dispute evidence; LLM output is drafts and query objects only.
Never mark anything paid from an unverified webhook.
Never invent a PayPal id outside DEMO_MODE; demo ids are visibly prefixed FAKE-.
Never commit secrets: keys stay in backend/.env (PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID, PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET, PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID).
Never push, open a PR or merge unless the user asks.

acceptance.check: Locking a verified listing with a simulated $15 capture creates exactly one invoice whose total is deposit + brokerage - 15, even if the worker runs twice.
An invoice amount that differs from the signed audit is refused unless a manager override with a note exists.
A replayed or unverified webhook changes nothing; a verified INVOICING.INVOICE.PAID marks the invoice and closing PAID once.
The ledger cockpit's totals equal the sum of ledger entries for every closing.
"Which deposits are unpaid after 3 days?" returns the right rows; "cancel all invoices" is refused.
A dispute produces an evidence pack whose every claim cites a record id, and nothing is submitted without approval.
backend: .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q passes; frontend: npm run build passes.

workflow.step: Read the files in read_first. Restate the plan in five lines and list any decision marked (proposed) in the plan; ask the user to confirm them before Phase 1.
Work phase by phase in order. Before each step, say what you will build; after it, run the tests, write the BUILD_LOG entry, and commit.
If a PayPal response shape differs from the plan, follow the real API, update the plan file, and note it in BUILD_LOG.
When blocked by a missing key or an unbuilt dependency, use the Fake/Demo path, say so, and keep going.
Finish with a short report: what is done and verified, what is not, and the commands to run the demo.

task.output_format: Short progress notes in plain English. Code in the repository, not in chat. Final report: done and verified, not done, how to run, open questions.
